description: Analyze thermal properties of a material: prepare samples, run DSC, TGA, and DMA measurements, interpret transitions, compare against references, and produce the thermal analysis report.

steps.description: Prepare samples for thermal analysis by selecting geometry, mass, and crucible type appropriate for each instrument.

inputs.name: material-description
inputs.desc: Identity and form of the material to analyze

inputs.name: analysis-objectives
inputs.desc: Which thermal properties are needed (Tg, Tm, Td, modulus)

outputs.name: sample-prep-protocol
outputs.desc: Step-by-step sample preparation instructions per instrument

outputs.name: instrument-queue
outputs.desc: Ordered list of instruments to run and their configurations

process: Identify the material type (polymer, ceramic, metal, composite) and select appropriate crucible and atmosphere.
Calculate target sample mass for each instrument based on expected heat flow and sensitivity.
Specify cutting, grinding, or molding steps to achieve the required sample geometry.
Define storage and handling conditions to prevent moisture uptake or degradation before measurement.

steps.description: Run differential scanning calorimetry to measure glass transition, melting, crystallization, and cure behavior.

inputs.name: instrument-queue
inputs.desc: DSC configuration from the prep step

outputs.name: dsc-thermogram
outputs.desc: Heat flow vs temperature curve with labeled transitions

outputs.name: dsc-parameters
outputs.desc: Extracted values: Tg, Tm, Tc, enthalpy of fusion, degree of crystallinity

process: Load the sample and reference into the DSC cell, seal the crucible, and purge with the specified gas.
Run the programmed temperature ramp (heat-cool-heat cycle for polymers, single ramp for metals).
Identify endothermic and exothermic events on the thermogram.
Extract onset, midpoint, and peak temperatures for each transition and compute enthalpies by integration.

steps.description: Run thermogravimetric analysis to measure decomposition temperature, mass loss steps, and residue content.

outputs.name: tga-curve
outputs.desc: Mass loss vs temperature curve with derivative (DTG)

outputs.name: tga-parameters
outputs.desc: Onset of decomposition, mass loss per step, residue percentage

process: Load the sample into the TGA pan and tare the balance.
Run the temperature program under specified atmosphere (nitrogen for decomposition, air for oxidation).
Compute the derivative thermogravimetry (DTG) curve to resolve overlapping mass loss steps.
Determine onset temperature, inflection point, and residue mass at final temperature.

steps.description: Run dynamic mechanical analysis to measure storage modulus, loss modulus, and tan delta as a function of temperature.

inputs.name: dsc-parameters
inputs.desc: Known transition temperatures to guide the DMA temperature range

outputs.name: dma-curves
outputs.desc: Storage modulus, loss modulus, and tan delta vs temperature

outputs.name: dma-parameters
outputs.desc: Glassy and rubbery modulus, Tg by tan delta peak, damping characteristics

process: Mount the specimen in the appropriate clamp geometry (single cantilever, dual cantilever, tension, three-point bend).
Set oscillation frequency, strain amplitude, and temperature ramp rate.
Run the temperature sweep and record storage modulus (E'), loss modulus (E''), and tan delta.
Identify the Tg as the tan delta peak and note any secondary relaxations.

steps.description: Interpret all thermal transitions across DSC, TGA, and DMA data to build a consistent picture of the material's thermal behavior.

inputs.name: tga-parameters
inputs.desc: TGA decomposition temperatures and mass losses

outputs.name: thermal-profile
outputs.desc: Unified thermal property summary with cross-validated transition temperatures

outputs.name: discrepancy-notes
outputs.desc: Any conflicts between instruments and likely explanations

process: Compare Tg values from DSC (midpoint) and DMA (tan delta peak) and note the expected offset.
Cross-check decomposition onset from TGA against any exothermic events in DSC.
Correlate modulus drop in DMA with the glass transition region from DSC.
Flag any unexpected transitions or mass losses that suggest contamination, moisture, or side reactions.

steps.description: Compare measured thermal properties against literature values and reference materials to validate the results.

outputs.name: reference-comparison-table
outputs.desc: Side-by-side measured vs literature values with sources

outputs.name: conformance-assessment
outputs.desc: Whether the material meets specification or matches expected grade

process: Look up published thermal property data for the material grade in handbooks and databases.
Build a comparison table: measured vs reference for each property (Tg, Tm, Td, modulus).
Flag deviations beyond expected measurement uncertainty.
Assess whether deviations indicate a different grade, aging, or processing history.

steps.description: Compile all thermal measurements into a structured report with methods, data, interpretation, and conclusions.

inputs.name: discrepancy-notes
inputs.desc: Any instrument conflicts or unexpected findings

outputs.name: thermal-analysis-report
outputs.desc: Complete report with figures, tables, methods, and conclusions

outputs.name: data-archive-package
outputs.desc: Raw data files, processed curves, and metadata for archival

process: Write the methods section covering instrument models, calibration dates, sample preparation, and measurement parameters.
Include annotated thermograms, TGA curves, and DMA plots as figures.
Present the reference comparison table and discuss any discrepancies.
State conclusions about the material's thermal suitability for its intended application.

description: Analyze NMR or MRI data: acquire raw spectra or images, process and correct, assign peaks or segment regions, quantify, compare against standards, and produce the analysis report.

steps.description: Plan the magnetic resonance acquisition: select the experiment type, pulse sequence, and acquisition parameters.

inputs.name: sample-or-subject
inputs.desc: Description of the sample (NMR) or subject (MRI)

inputs.name: analysis-question
inputs.desc: What structural or spatial information is needed

outputs.name: acquisition-protocol
outputs.desc: Pulse sequence, parameters, and expected run time

outputs.name: raw-mr-data
outputs.desc: Free induction decay (NMR) or k-space data (MRI)

process: Select the nucleus (1H, 13C, 31P for NMR) or contrast weighting (T1, T2, diffusion for MRI).
Choose the pulse sequence and set repetition time, echo time, spectral width, and number of scans.
Acquire the data and verify signal-to-noise ratio meets the analysis requirements.
Export the raw data in a standard format (JCAMP-DX for NMR, DICOM for MRI).

steps.description: Process raw magnetic resonance data: Fourier transform, phase correction, baseline correction, and apodization.

outputs.name: processed-spectrum-or-image
outputs.desc: Frequency-domain spectrum or reconstructed image

outputs.name: processing-log
outputs.desc: Record of every processing step and parameter applied

process: Apply apodization (exponential or Gaussian window) to improve signal-to-noise.
Perform Fourier transformation to convert time-domain to frequency-domain.
Correct zero-order and first-order phase errors.
Flatten the baseline using polynomial or spline fitting.

steps.description: Assign peaks in an NMR spectrum to molecular fragments, or segment regions in an MRI dataset.

inputs.name: processed-spectrum-or-image
inputs.desc: Processed NMR spectrum or MRI image

inputs.name: sample-or-subject
inputs.desc: Known or expected molecular structure or anatomy

outputs.name: assignment-table
outputs.desc: Peak-to-structure assignments (NMR) or region labels (MRI)

outputs.name: unassigned-features
outputs.desc: Any peaks or regions that could not be confidently assigned

process: For NMR: identify chemical shift ranges and match to functional groups using reference tables.
For NMR: use splitting patterns and coupling constants to confirm connectivity.
For MRI: segment regions of interest using threshold, atlas-based, or machine learning approaches.
Flag any unexpected peaks or regions that may indicate impurities, artifacts, or pathology.

steps.description: Quantify peak integrals (NMR) or region volumes (MRI) to extract concentrations, ratios, or sizes.

inputs.name: assignment-table
inputs.desc: Which peaks or regions to quantify

outputs.name: quantification-results
outputs.desc: Concentrations, molar ratios, or volumetric measurements

outputs.name: measurement-uncertainty
outputs.desc: Uncertainty estimates for each quantified value

process: For NMR: integrate assigned peaks and normalize to an internal standard or reference peak.
For MRI: compute volumes of segmented regions by voxel counting and correct for partial volume effects.
Calculate concentrations or molar ratios from integral ratios.
Estimate measurement uncertainty from signal-to-noise, integration limits, and segmentation variability.

steps.description: Compare measured chemical shifts, relaxation times, or volumes against published standards and atlases.

outputs.name: standards-comparison-table
outputs.desc: Measured vs reference values with literature sources

outputs.name: deviation-flags
outputs.desc: Values that fall outside expected ranges

process: Look up reference chemical shifts, relaxation times, or normative volumes in published databases.
Compute the deviation between measured and reference values.
Flag values outside the expected range, accounting for instrument, solvent, and field strength differences.
Note any findings that may require follow-up experiments or clinical correlation.

steps.description: Compile the magnetic resonance analysis into a report with methods, spectra or images, assignments, quantification, and conclusions.

outputs.name: mr-analysis-report
outputs.desc: Complete report with annotated spectra/images and conclusions

outputs.name: raw-data-package
outputs.desc: Raw and processed data for archival

process: Write the methods section: instrument, field strength, pulse sequence, processing parameters.
Include annotated spectra or images with labeled peaks or regions.
Present quantification results and reference comparisons in tables.
State conclusions about molecular structure, purity, composition, or anatomical findings.

description: Quantify features in optical microscopy images: capture with consistent settings, correct illumination, segment features, measure morphometrics, compute statistics, and produce the quantification report.

steps.description: Capture microscopy images with consistent illumination, focus, and exposure settings across all fields of view.

inputs.name: specimen-description
inputs.desc: What is being imaged and at what magnification

inputs.name: quantification-targets
inputs.desc: Which features need to be measured (size, count, shape, intensity)

outputs.name: image-set
outputs.desc: Set of captured images with metadata (magnification, pixel size, exposure)

outputs.name: capture-protocol
outputs.desc: Settings used for reproducibility

process: Set up Kohler illumination and white balance for consistent lighting.
Select magnification and verify pixel-to-micrometer calibration with a stage micrometer.
Capture images at randomly selected or systematically spaced fields of view.
Record all acquisition parameters for the protocol.

steps.description: Correct for uneven illumination (vignetting, shading) across the field of view.

outputs.name: corrected-images
outputs.desc: Flat-field corrected images

outputs.name: correction-quality-metrics
outputs.desc: Uniformity measures before and after correction

process: Acquire or generate a flat-field reference image (empty field with same illumination).
Divide each image by the flat-field reference to normalize illumination.
Verify correction by checking intensity uniformity across the field.
Apply background subtraction if needed for fluorescence images.

steps.description: Segment features of interest from the background using threshold, watershed, or machine learning methods.

outputs.name: segmentation-masks
outputs.desc: Binary or labeled masks identifying each feature instance

outputs.name: segmentation-parameters
outputs.desc: Method and thresholds used

process: Select the segmentation approach based on contrast: global threshold, adaptive threshold, or watershed for touching objects.
Apply morphological operations (opening, closing) to clean the mask.
Separate touching features using watershed or distance transform.
Visually verify segmentation on a subset and adjust parameters if needed.

steps.description: Measure size, shape, and intensity of each segmented feature.

inputs.name: corrected-images
inputs.desc: Original intensity images for intensity measurements

outputs.name: feature-measurements
outputs.desc: Per-feature table: area, perimeter, circularity, aspect ratio, mean intensity

outputs.name: measurement-units
outputs.desc: Calibration applied (micrometers, pixels)

process: For each labeled region, compute area, perimeter, bounding box, centroid.
Calculate shape descriptors: circularity, aspect ratio, solidity, eccentricity.
Measure mean, median, and standard deviation of intensity within each region.
Apply pixel-to-micrometer calibration to convert measurements to physical units.

steps.description: Compute summary statistics across all fields of view: means, distributions, and sample-level estimates.

inputs.name: image-set
inputs.desc: Image metadata for grouping by field

outputs.name: summary-statistics
outputs.desc: Mean, SD, median, range for each metric; feature count per field

outputs.name: distribution-plots
outputs.desc: Histograms and box plots of key measurements

process: Pool measurements across all fields of view.
Compute descriptive statistics: mean, standard deviation, median, interquartile range.
Generate histograms to visualize the distribution of sizes, shapes, and intensities.
Report feature density (count per unit area) with confidence intervals.

steps.description: Compile the microscopy quantification into a report with methods, representative images, measurements, and conclusions.

outputs.name: quantification-report
outputs.desc: Complete microscopy quantification report

outputs.name: analysis-archive
outputs.desc: Images, masks, measurement tables, and scripts for reproducibility

process: Write methods: specimen preparation, imaging parameters, segmentation approach, measurement definitions.
Include representative images with overlaid segmentation for quality verification.
Present summary statistics and distributions in tables and figures.
State conclusions about the specimen's microstructure and note any limitations.

description: Interpolate between sample points in a geographic area: import data, explore spatial patterns, select and run the interpolation method, cross-validate, and produce the interpolation map with uncertainty.

steps.description: Import point-sampled data with coordinates, reproject to a common coordinate system, and assess spatial coverage.

inputs.name: sample-data-file
inputs.desc: CSV, shapefile, or GeoJSON with coordinates and measured values

inputs.name: study-area-boundary
inputs.desc: Polygon defining the area to interpolate within

outputs.name: projected-point-dataset
outputs.desc: Point data in a consistent projected coordinate system

outputs.name: coverage-assessment
outputs.desc: Map of sample density and gaps in coverage

process: Read the input data and parse coordinates and attribute values.
Reproject all points to a common projected coordinate system (UTM or state plane).
Clip points to the study area boundary.
Map sample density and identify areas with sparse coverage that will have higher interpolation uncertainty.

steps.description: Explore spatial autocorrelation by computing and modeling the experimental variogram.

inputs.name: projected-point-dataset
inputs.desc: Georeferenced sample points with measured values

outputs.name: variogram-model
outputs.desc: Fitted variogram model (spherical, exponential, Gaussian) with sill, range, and nugget

outputs.name: spatial-correlation-summary
outputs.desc: Description of how the variable changes with distance

process: Compute the experimental variogram at multiple lag distances.
Test directional variograms to check for anisotropy.
Fit theoretical variogram models (spherical, exponential, Gaussian) and select by least squares.
Extract the nugget (measurement noise), sill (total variance), and range (correlation distance).

steps.description: Select the interpolation method based on data characteristics, variogram results, and analysis requirements.

outputs.name: selected-method
outputs.desc: Chosen interpolation method with parameters (kriging type, IDW power, spline tension)

outputs.name: method-justification
outputs.desc: Why this method fits the data and analysis goals

process: If a clear variogram structure exists, select ordinary or universal kriging for optimal estimation with uncertainty.
If sample count is small or variogram is noisy, consider IDW or radial basis functions as alternatives.
If the variable has a known trend (e.g., elevation-dependent temperature), select universal kriging or regression kriging.
Document the method choice and parameter settings.

steps.description: Run the selected interpolation to generate a continuous raster surface over the study area.

outputs.name: interpolated-surface
outputs.desc: Raster grid of predicted values

outputs.name: prediction-uncertainty
outputs.desc: Kriging variance or other uncertainty surface if available

process: Define the output raster grid resolution based on sample density and analysis needs.
Run the interpolation algorithm over the study area.
If kriging, also generate the kriging variance surface as a measure of prediction uncertainty.
Clip the output to the study area boundary.

steps.description: Validate the interpolation using leave-one-out cross-validation to assess prediction accuracy.

outputs.name: cross-validation-metrics
outputs.desc: RMSE, MAE, mean error, and R-squared from leave-one-out

outputs.name: residual-map
outputs.desc: Spatial distribution of prediction errors

process: For each sample point, remove it, interpolate from remaining points, and record the prediction error.
Compute summary error metrics: RMSE, MAE, mean error (bias), and R-squared.
Map residuals spatially to check for systematic patterns in the errors.
If errors show spatial patterns, revisit the variogram or method choice.

steps.description: Produce the interpolation map, uncertainty surface, and report documenting methods, validation, and results.

outputs.name: interpolation-map
outputs.desc: Final map with contours, color ramp, and legend

outputs.name: interpolation-report
outputs.desc: Report with methods, variogram, validation, and interpretation

process: Generate the final map with appropriate color ramp, contour lines, and legend.
Overlay the uncertainty surface to show where predictions are most and least reliable.
Write the methods section covering data sources, variogram modeling, interpolation, and validation.
Discuss cross-validation results and state the spatial resolution and confidence of the predictions.

description: Analyze DNA methylation patterns from bisulfite sequencing: quality control, alignment, methylation calling, differential analysis, genomic annotation, and reporting.

steps.description: Quality-control bisulfite sequencing reads: adapter trimming, quality filtering, and bisulfite conversion rate assessment.

inputs.name: sample-metadata
inputs.desc: Sample names, conditions, and expected conversion controls

outputs.name: trimmed-reads
outputs.desc: Quality-filtered and adapter-trimmed FASTQ files

outputs.name: qc-summary
outputs.desc: Read quality metrics and bisulfite conversion rate per sample

process: Run quality assessment on raw reads (per-base quality, adapter content, duplication rate).
Trim adapters and low-quality bases from read ends.
Estimate bisulfite conversion rate from spike-in controls or non-CpG methylation levels.
Flag samples with conversion rate below 99% for potential exclusion.

steps.description: Align bisulfite-converted reads to a reference genome using a bisulfite-aware aligner.

outputs.name: aligned-reads
outputs.desc: BAM files with aligned bisulfite reads

outputs.name: alignment-statistics
outputs.desc: Mapping rate, duplication rate, coverage per sample

process: Align using a bisulfite-aware aligner (Bismark, bwa-meth, or BSMAP).
Remove PCR duplicates based on alignment position.
Compute alignment statistics: mapping rate, insert size distribution, genome coverage.
Verify that coverage is sufficient for the analysis (typically 10x or higher for single-CpG resolution).

steps.description: Call methylation levels at individual CpG sites from aligned bisulfite reads.

outputs.name: cpg-methylation-table
outputs.desc: Per-CpG methylation level (beta value) and coverage per sample

outputs.name: genome-wide-methylation-summary
outputs.desc: Overall methylation level distribution and CpG island vs open sea statistics

process: Extract methylation calls at each CpG site (count of methylated and unmethylated reads).
Compute beta values (methylated / total) and filter sites below minimum coverage threshold.
Summarize genome-wide methylation distribution and stratify by genomic context (CpG island, shore, shelf, open sea).
Generate a methylation density plot to visualize the bimodal distribution.

steps.description: Identify differentially methylated regions (DMRs) between conditions or groups.

inputs.name: cpg-methylation-table
inputs.desc: Per-CpG methylation levels across all samples

outputs.name: dmr-list
outputs.desc: Regions with significant methylation differences, with coordinates, effect size, and p-values

outputs.name: dmr-statistics
outputs.desc: Number of hyper- and hypo-methylated DMRs, effect size distribution

process: Select the DMR detection method (BSmooth, DMRseq, or methylKit) based on sample count and design.
Run the analysis with appropriate multiple testing correction.
Filter DMRs by minimum number of CpGs, minimum effect size, and adjusted p-value threshold.
Classify DMRs as hyper-methylated or hypo-methylated relative to the reference group.

steps.description: Annotate DMRs with genomic features: promoters, enhancers, gene bodies, CpG islands, and regulatory elements.

outputs.name: annotated-dmr-list
outputs.desc: DMRs with overlapping genes, promoters, enhancers, and regulatory annotations

outputs.name: enrichment-results
outputs.desc: Enrichment of DMRs in specific genomic features vs background

process: Overlap DMRs with gene annotations (TSS, gene body, intergenic).
Annotate with CpG island context (island, shore, shelf, open sea).
Overlap with chromatin state maps or enhancer databases if available.
Test for enrichment of DMRs in specific genomic features compared to all tested CpGs.

steps.description: Assess biological significance of methylation changes through pathway analysis and integration with expression data.

inputs.name: annotated-dmr-list
inputs.desc: DMRs with gene and feature annotations

outputs.name: pathway-analysis-results
outputs.desc: Enriched pathways and gene ontology terms among DMR-associated genes

outputs.name: biological-interpretation
outputs.desc: Summary of which biological processes are affected by methylation changes

process: Extract genes associated with DMRs (promoter or gene body overlap).
Run gene ontology and pathway enrichment analysis (KEGG, Reactome).
If expression data is available, correlate methylation changes with expression changes at the same genes.
Summarize the biological processes most affected by the observed methylation differences.

steps.description: Compile the DNA methylation analysis into a report with QC, methods, DMR results, annotations, and biological interpretation.

outputs.name: methylation-report
outputs.desc: Complete epigenomics analysis report

outputs.name: supplementary-tables
outputs.desc: Full DMR list, annotations, and pathway results for download

process: Present QC metrics, alignment statistics, and conversion rates.
Show genome-wide methylation patterns and DMR summary statistics.
Include volcano plots, heatmaps of top DMRs, and genomic distribution plots.
Discuss biological significance, pathway enrichment, and study limitations.

description: Test friction and wear properties: select the test configuration, set conditions, run the test, measure wear and friction, compare across materials, and produce the tribology report.

steps.description: Select the tribology test configuration and conditions to match the application's contact geometry, load, speed, and environment.

inputs.name: application-conditions
inputs.desc: Load, speed, temperature, lubrication, and contact type in the real application

inputs.name: materials-to-test
inputs.desc: List of material pairs (surface and counter-body) to evaluate

outputs.name: test-configuration
outputs.desc: Pin-on-disk, ball-on-flat, reciprocating, or block-on-ring with all parameters

outputs.name: test-matrix
outputs.desc: Number of replicates, material combinations, and condition variations

process: Match the application contact type to a standard test geometry (ASTM G99, G133, or similar).
Select load, speed, and sliding distance to represent the application or to standardize for comparison.
Specify the environment (ambient air, controlled humidity, temperature, or lubricant).
Define the number of replicates per condition for statistical confidence.

steps.description: Prepare test specimens to controlled surface finish and geometry for reproducible tribology measurements.

inputs.name: materials-to-test
inputs.desc: Materials and their forms (disk, pin, ball, block)

inputs.name: test-configuration
inputs.desc: Required specimen dimensions and surface finish

outputs.name: prepared-specimens
outputs.desc: Specimens with documented surface roughness and dimensions

outputs.name: pre-test-surface-data
outputs.desc: Surface roughness profiles and optical micrographs before testing

process: Machine or cut specimens to the required dimensions.
Polish to the target surface roughness (Ra) and verify with a profilometer.
Clean specimens using an ultrasonic bath with solvent to remove contamination.
Document pre-test surface roughness and photograph the surface.

steps.description: Run the tribology test with continuous friction force and contact data acquisition.

outputs.name: friction-time-series
outputs.desc: Friction force or coefficient vs sliding distance or time

outputs.name: test-conditions-log
outputs.desc: Actual temperature, humidity, and any anomalies during the test

process: Mount the specimen and counter-body, apply the specified load, and start the motion.
Record friction force continuously throughout the test at the specified sampling rate.
Monitor and log environmental conditions (temperature, humidity) during the test.
Stop at the target sliding distance or time and carefully remove specimens for post-test analysis.

steps.description: Measure wear volume, surface roughness, and morphology after the tribology test.

outputs.name: wear-measurements
outputs.desc: Wear volume, specific wear rate, and post-test surface roughness

outputs.name: wear-morphology
outputs.desc: Optical and SEM images of wear tracks showing the dominant wear mechanism

process: Profile the wear track or scar using a profilometer or optical interferometer.
Compute wear volume from the track cross-section and length (or mass loss if measured).
Calculate the specific wear rate: volume lost per unit load per unit sliding distance.
Image the wear track to identify the wear mechanism (abrasive, adhesive, oxidative, fatigue).

steps.description: Compare friction and wear results across material pairs and conditions.

outputs.name: comparison-table
outputs.desc: Friction coefficient and wear rate for each material pair and condition

outputs.name: ranking
outputs.desc: Materials ranked by tribological performance

process: Extract steady-state friction coefficient from each test (excluding the run-in period).
Tabulate friction coefficient and specific wear rate with standard deviations across replicates.
Rank materials by the performance metric most relevant to the application.
Identify any friction transitions, seizure events, or unexpected behavior.

steps.description: Compile the tribology study into a report with test methods, friction curves, wear data, comparisons, and recommendations.

outputs.name: tribology-report
outputs.desc: Complete tribology testing report with figures and recommendations

outputs.name: raw-data-archive
outputs.desc: Friction time series, profilometry files, and images

process: Write the methods section: test standard, geometry, parameters, specimen preparation, and instrumentation.
Include friction vs distance plots and representative wear track images.
Present the comparison table and material ranking.
Recommend the material pair that best meets the application's friction and wear requirements.

description: Optimize a fermentation process: define the target, screen media, design experiments, run fermentations with monitoring, model the response, and produce the optimization report.

steps.description: Define the fermentation target product, organism, and baseline conditions to optimize from.

inputs.name: target-product
inputs.desc: What the fermentation should produce (metabolite, protein, biomass)

inputs.name: organism-strain
inputs.desc: The production organism and its known requirements

outputs.name: baseline-conditions
outputs.desc: Current best-known media, temperature, pH, aeration for this organism and product

outputs.name: optimization-objectives
outputs.desc: Which responses to maximize or minimize (titer, yield, productivity, cost)

process: Review the literature for the organism's growth requirements and known production conditions.
Establish baseline conditions from published protocols or prior runs.
Define the optimization objective: maximize titer, yield (product per substrate), or volumetric productivity.
Identify constraints: pH range, temperature limits, dissolved oxygen requirements, and cost limits.

steps.description: Screen media components to identify which carbon, nitrogen, and mineral sources most affect the target product.

outputs.name: significant-components
outputs.desc: Media components with the largest effect on the target product

outputs.name: screening-data
outputs.desc: Titer and growth data from the screening experiment

process: Design a Plackett-Burman or fractional factorial screening experiment covering 8-12 media components.
Run the screening fermentations (small scale, typically shake flasks).
Measure the target product titer and biomass for each condition.
Analyze main effects to identify the 3-5 most significant components for further optimization.

steps.description: Design the response surface experiment to optimize the significant media components and process parameters.

outputs.name: experimental-design
outputs.desc: Central composite or Box-Behnken design with run list and center points

outputs.name: factor-ranges
outputs.desc: Low, center, and high levels for each factor

process: Select the design type: central composite design (CCD) or Box-Behnken based on the number of factors.
Set factor ranges based on screening results and biological constraints.
Include center point replicates for curvature estimation and pure error.
Randomize the run order to minimize time-dependent bias.

steps.description: Run the designed fermentations with continuous monitoring of growth, pH, dissolved oxygen, and product titer.

outputs.name: fermentation-time-courses
outputs.desc: OD, pH, DO, substrate, and product concentrations over time for each run

outputs.name: final-responses
outputs.desc: End-point titer, yield, and productivity for each design point

process: Prepare media according to each design point's composition.
Inoculate from a standardized seed culture and run fermentations under controlled conditions.
Sample at regular intervals for OD, pH, substrate consumption, and product titer.
Record dissolved oxygen and any pH or temperature excursions.

steps.description: Fit a response surface model to the fermentation data, identify the optimum, and validate it.

inputs.name: final-responses
inputs.desc: Titer, yield, productivity at each design point

outputs.name: response-surface-model
outputs.desc: Fitted quadratic model with coefficients, R-squared, and ANOVA

outputs.name: predicted-optimum
outputs.desc: Factor levels that maximize the objective, with predicted response and confidence interval

process: Fit a second-order polynomial model (main effects, interactions, quadratic terms).
Check model adequacy: R-squared, adjusted R-squared, lack-of-fit test, residual plots.
Locate the optimum by solving the response surface equations or by numerical search.
Report the predicted optimum conditions and expected response with confidence bounds.

steps.description: Compile the optimization study into a report with screening results, response surface analysis, optimal conditions, and validation.

outputs.name: optimization-report
outputs.desc: Complete fermentation optimization report

outputs.name: recommended-protocol
outputs.desc: Optimized media and process conditions ready for scale-up evaluation

process: Summarize the screening phase: which components mattered and which did not.
Present the response surface model, contour plots, and ANOVA table.
State the optimized conditions and the improvement over baseline.
Recommend validation runs and note considerations for scaling up.

description: Analyze single-cell RNA sequencing data: quality filter, normalize, find variable genes, reduce dimensions, cluster, identify markers, annotate cell types, and report.

steps.description: Filter cells and genes from a single-cell RNA-seq count matrix based on quality metrics.

inputs.name: count-matrix
inputs.desc: Raw gene-by-cell count matrix from Cell Ranger or similar

inputs.name: sample-metadata
inputs.desc: Sample identifiers, batch labels, and expected cell counts

outputs.name: filtered-matrix
outputs.desc: Count matrix with low-quality cells and uninformative genes removed

outputs.name: qc-metrics
outputs.desc: Distribution plots of genes per cell, UMIs per cell, and mitochondrial fraction

process: Compute per-cell QC metrics: number of detected genes, total UMI count, percent mitochondrial reads.
Set thresholds to remove empty droplets (low UMI), doublets (high UMI and gene count), and dying cells (high mito).
Remove genes detected in fewer than a minimum number of cells.
Report how many cells and genes remain after filtering.

steps.description: Normalize single-cell counts to correct for differences in sequencing depth across cells.

inputs.name: qc-metrics
inputs.desc: Cell-level QC data for informed normalization

outputs.name: normalized-matrix
outputs.desc: Log-normalized expression matrix

outputs.name: highly-variable-genes
outputs.desc: List of genes with high cell-to-cell variability for downstream analysis

process: Normalize each cell's counts by its total UMI count and scale to a target sum (e.g., 10,000).
Log-transform the normalized counts (log1p).
Identify highly variable genes using variance-to-mean ratio or similar method.
Select the top 2000-3000 highly variable genes for dimensionality reduction.

steps.description: Reduce the high-dimensional expression data to a low-dimensional representation using PCA followed by UMAP or t-SNE.

outputs.name: pca-embeddings
outputs.desc: Top principal components (typically 30-50)

outputs.name: umap-coordinates
outputs.desc: 2D UMAP embedding for visualization

process: Run PCA on the highly variable genes and select the number of components using an elbow plot.
Compute a k-nearest-neighbor graph from the PCA embeddings.
Run UMAP on the neighbor graph to produce a 2D visualization.
Color the UMAP by QC metrics to verify that structure is biological, not technical.

steps.description: Cluster cells into transcriptionally distinct groups using graph-based community detection.

inputs.name: pca-embeddings
inputs.desc: PCA coordinates for neighbor graph construction

outputs.name: cluster-assignments
outputs.desc: Cluster label for each cell

outputs.name: cluster-umap-plot
outputs.desc: UMAP colored by cluster identity

process: Construct a shared nearest-neighbor (SNN) graph from the PCA embeddings.
Run Leiden or Louvain community detection at one or more resolution parameters.
Visualize clusters on the UMAP and inspect for over- or under-clustering.
Adjust resolution and re-cluster if needed until clusters correspond to visually separable groups.

steps.description: Identify marker genes that distinguish each cluster from all other clusters.

inputs.name: cluster-assignments
inputs.desc: Which cells belong to which cluster

outputs.name: marker-gene-table
outputs.desc: Top marker genes per cluster with log fold change, p-value, and percent expressed

outputs.name: marker-heatmap
outputs.desc: Heatmap of top markers across clusters

process: For each cluster, run a differential expression test (Wilcoxon rank-sum or logistic regression) against all other cells.
Filter markers by minimum log fold change and adjusted p-value threshold.
Rank markers by a combined score of effect size and specificity.
Generate a heatmap showing the top 5-10 markers per cluster across all cells.

steps.description: Annotate clusters with cell type identities using marker genes, reference datasets, or automated classifiers.

outputs.name: cell-type-labels
outputs.desc: Cell type annotation for each cluster

outputs.name: annotation-confidence
outputs.desc: Confidence level for each annotation based on marker overlap and reference agreement

process: Compare top markers against known cell type markers from published databases (CellMarker, PanglaoDB).
If a reference atlas exists for the tissue, project cells onto the reference and transfer labels.
Assign cell type labels to clusters where markers unambiguously match a known type.
Flag clusters with ambiguous or novel marker profiles for further investigation.

steps.description: Compile the single-cell analysis into a report with QC, clustering, markers, cell types, and biological interpretation.

outputs.name: scrna-report
outputs.desc: Complete single-cell RNA-seq analysis report

outputs.name: processed-data-object
outputs.desc: Annotated AnnData or Seurat object for further analysis

process: Present QC filtering statistics and the effect on cell and gene counts.
Show the UMAP with cluster and cell type annotations.
Include the marker gene heatmap and a dot plot of top markers.
Discuss the cell type composition, any novel populations, and biological implications.

description: Test corrosion resistance: select the test method, prepare and expose specimens, measure corrosion rate by mass loss and electrochemistry, characterize products, and produce the corrosion report.

steps.description: Select the corrosion test method based on the application environment, material, and standards compliance requirements.

inputs.name: service-environment
inputs.desc: Exposure conditions in the application (salt water, acid, atmospheric, etc.)

outputs.name: selected-test-methods
outputs.desc: Salt spray (ASTM B117), electrochemical (ASTM G59/G61), immersion (ASTM G31), or cyclic

outputs.name: test-parameters
outputs.desc: Solution composition, temperature, duration, and electrode configuration

process: Match the service environment to the appropriate accelerated test standard.
Select salt spray for general atmospheric corrosion ranking, electrochemical for mechanism and rate data, immersion for uniform corrosion rate.
Define test duration, solution chemistry, and temperature.
Specify the number of replicates per material for statistical analysis.

steps.description: Prepare corrosion test specimens to a defined surface condition and document initial mass and dimensions.

inputs.name: test-parameters
inputs.desc: Specimen geometry requirements for the test method

outputs.name: prepared-corrosion-specimens
outputs.desc: Specimens with measured initial mass, area, and surface finish

outputs.name: pre-exposure-documentation
outputs.desc: Photographs and surface condition records

process: Cut specimens to the required dimensions and grind to a uniform surface finish.
Clean with solvent, rinse, and dry to a constant weight.
Measure and record initial mass (to 0.1 mg), exposed surface area, and dimensions.
Photograph the surface and apply masking to non-test areas if needed.

steps.description: Expose specimens and run electrochemical measurements: open circuit potential, polarization curves, and impedance spectroscopy.

outputs.name: electrochemical-data
outputs.desc: OCP vs time, polarization curves, and EIS spectra

outputs.name: mass-loss-data
outputs.desc: Post-exposure mass after cleaning off corrosion products

process: For electrochemical tests: mount the specimen as the working electrode, immerse, and stabilize the open circuit potential.
Run potentiodynamic polarization to get corrosion potential and corrosion current density.
Run electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) to characterize the corrosion interface.
For immersion or salt spray: expose for the specified duration, then clean and weigh to determine mass loss.

steps.description: Characterize the corrosion products and attack morphology using microscopy and spectroscopy.

outputs.name: corrosion-morphology
outputs.desc: Optical and SEM images showing pit depth, intergranular attack, or uniform thinning

outputs.name: product-composition
outputs.desc: EDS or XRD identification of corrosion product phases

process: Examine the corroded surface under optical microscopy at low and high magnification.
Image representative areas under SEM for higher resolution morphology.
Run EDS on corrosion products to identify elemental composition.
Classify the corrosion form: uniform, pitting, crevice, intergranular, galvanic, or stress corrosion cracking.

steps.description: Calculate corrosion rates from mass loss and electrochemical data and rank materials.

outputs.name: corrosion-rates
outputs.desc: Corrosion rate in mm/year from mass loss and from Tafel extrapolation

outputs.name: material-ranking
outputs.desc: Materials ranked by corrosion resistance with statistical confidence

process: Calculate mass loss corrosion rate: (mass loss * K) / (area * time * density), where K converts to mm/year.
Extract corrosion current density from Tafel extrapolation and convert to mm/year using Faraday's law.
Compare mass loss and electrochemical rates and note any discrepancy (passivation, localized attack).
Rank materials and report mean and standard deviation across replicates.

steps.description: Compile the corrosion study into a report with methods, electrochemical data, mass loss, morphology, and material ranking.

outputs.name: corrosion-report
outputs.desc: Complete corrosion testing report

outputs.name: data-archive
outputs.desc: Electrochemical files, mass data, and images

process: Write methods: test standards, solution chemistry, parameters, specimen preparation, and instrumentation.
Include polarization curves, EIS Nyquist plots, and corroded surface images.
Present corrosion rates and material ranking in a comparison table.
Recommend the material best suited for the service environment.

description: Model drug pharmacokinetics: compile concentration-time data, select a compartmental model, estimate PK parameters, assess fit, simulate dosing regimens, and produce the PK report.

steps.description: Compile drug concentration-time data from dosing studies, merge with dosing records, and assess data quality.

inputs.name: concentration-time-data
inputs.desc: Measured drug concentrations at sampled time points

inputs.name: dosing-records
inputs.desc: Dose amounts, routes, and timing for each subject

outputs.name: pk-dataset
outputs.desc: Merged concentration-time-dose dataset ready for modeling

outputs.name: data-quality-flags
outputs.desc: Flagged outliers, BLQ values, and missing time points

process: Merge concentration measurements with dosing records by subject and time.
Handle below-the-limit-of-quantification (BLQ) values using an appropriate method (LLOQ/2, likelihood-based).
Identify and flag potential outliers based on concentration-time profile inspection.
Plot individual concentration-time profiles on a semi-log scale for visual assessment.

steps.description: Select the compartmental PK model structure: one-compartment, two-compartment, or population approach.

inputs.name: dosing-records
inputs.desc: Route of administration determines absorption model

outputs.name: model-structure
outputs.desc: Selected model: number of compartments, absorption model, elimination model

outputs.name: initial-parameter-estimates
outputs.desc: Starting values for model fitting

process: Inspect the semi-log concentration-time plot: a single straight line suggests one-compartment, a biexponential curve suggests two.
For oral dosing, add a first-order absorption compartment with or without lag time.
For population PK, define the structural model, then specify random effects for inter-individual variability.
Set initial parameter estimates from published values or non-compartmental analysis.

steps.description: Fit the PK model to the data and estimate pharmacokinetic parameters.

outputs.name: fitted-parameters
outputs.desc: Estimated PK parameters: CL, Vd, ka, half-life, with standard errors

outputs.name: model-diagnostics
outputs.desc: Objective function value, parameter precision, and convergence status

process: Run the parameter estimation using maximum likelihood (individual) or FOCE/SAEM (population).
Verify convergence: successful minimization, no boundary hits, reasonable parameter precision.
Compute derived parameters: half-life from CL and Vd, AUC from model predictions.
If the model does not converge, simplify the model or adjust initial estimates.

steps.description: Assess model adequacy using diagnostic plots and statistical tests.

outputs.name: gof-plots
outputs.desc: Observed vs predicted, residuals vs time, residuals vs predicted, QQ plot

outputs.name: model-adequacy-assessment
outputs.desc: Whether the model adequately describes the data

process: Generate observed vs population-predicted and observed vs individual-predicted plots.
Plot conditional weighted residuals (CWRES) vs time and vs predicted concentration.
Check for systematic trends in residuals that indicate model misspecification.
For population models, inspect individual fits for poorly described subjects.

steps.description: Simulate drug concentration profiles under alternative dosing regimens to support dose selection.

outputs.name: simulated-profiles
outputs.desc: Predicted concentration-time curves for each dosing regimen

outputs.name: dosing-comparison-table
outputs.desc: Cmax, Cmin, AUC, and time above target for each regimen

process: Define candidate dosing regimens: dose amounts, intervals, and durations.
Simulate concentration-time profiles at steady state for each regimen.
Compute summary PK metrics: Cmax, Cmin (trough), AUC per interval, time above a pharmacological target.
For population models, simulate with inter-individual variability to show expected population range.

steps.description: Compile the pharmacokinetics analysis into a report with data summary, model development, diagnostics, simulations, and dosing recommendations.

outputs.name: pk-report
outputs.desc: Complete pharmacokinetic modeling report

outputs.name: model-code-archive
outputs.desc: Model code, datasets, and output files for reproducibility

process: Summarize the study data: number of subjects, samples, dose levels, and sampling scheme.
Present the model development: structural model, covariate analysis (if population), and final parameters.
Include all diagnostic plots and discuss model adequacy.
Present dosing simulations and make recommendations based on the target therapeutic window.
